neighbours.label: the word that sets up a comparison of someone against rivals or peers (below their peers, an edge over others, ahead of her competitor, rivaled by); the same sentence without a compared-to group stays quiet
fire: On the exam, rural pupils scored far below their classmates in the city.
The new phone stays well ahead of its nearest rival on battery life.
His speed on the bike is matched only by a handful of riders in Europe.
Good references can give a candidate an advantage over the other finalists.
She crossed the line a full lap ahead of her nearest challenger.
Parents should avoid comparing a child to her cousins at family dinners.
The small brewery now outsells its larger competitors in the region.
Their profits lag far behind those of their main competitors.
quiet: On the exam, rural pupils scored well on the reading section.
The new phone has a large screen and a long battery life.
His speed on the bike improved a lot during the spring.
Good references can help a candidate during the final interview.
She crossed the line and waved to her family in the stands.
